title: EA-Bench: Measuring information and action efficiency under imperfect instructions
abstract: arXiv:2611.28846v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Personal agents help users complete everyday work across digital applications. Many standard benchmarks assume that users provide sufficient information to solve a task. However, agents often encounter incomplete, distracting, or inconsistent information in practice. To systematically study agent inefficiency under such imperfect information, we introduce Efficient Action (EA)-Bench, which evaluates both tool calls and user interactions in work-related tasks. To our knowledge, it is the first benchmark to jointly evaluate tool-call efficiency and user-interaction efficiency under controlled missing, redundant, and conflicting information. We construct 63 base-task instances adapted from existing work-related benchmarks. translated_title: EA-Bench：在不完美指令下测量信息与动作效率
translated_abstract: 个人智能体（Personal agents）帮助用户在各类数字应用中完成日常工作。许多标准基准测试假设用户会提供解决任务所需的充分信息，然而在实践中，智能体经常遇到不完整、干扰性或不一致的信息。为了系统地研究智能体在此类不完美信息下的低效问题，我们引入了高效动作（Efficient Action, EA）基准，用于评估工作相关任务中的工具调用与用户交互。据我们所知，这是首个在受控的缺失、冗余和冲突信息条件下，联合评估工具调用效率与用户交互效率的基准。我们从现有工作相关基准中改编构建了63个基础任务实例。为了指导扰动设计并量化任务需求，我们将工作流表示为有向无环图（DAG），并通过分析节点级依赖关系，确定信息可以在何处被隐瞒、反驳或补充。
tldr: 该论文提出了EA-Bench，这是首个在受控的缺失、冗余和冲突信息等不完美指令条件下，联合评估个人智能体工具调用效率与用户交互效率的基准，并通过将工作流建模为有向无环图（DAG）来指导信息扰动设计与任务需求量化。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces EA-Bench, the first benchmark that jointly evaluates tool-call efficiency and user-interaction efficiency of personal agents under controlled missing, redundant, and conflicting information, representing workflows as directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) to guide perturbation design and quantify task requirements.
